2026-10.headline: Rule-based picks after diligence and a skeptical red-team pass (27 Oct): 18 committee-shortlist longs, 35 other top longs, 3 top short and 8 pair shorts (diligence-confirmed short legs), plus 9 analyst nominees. Red-teaming the ten highest-conviction longs demoted 47 of them: elite status now requires surviving the strongest bear case, not just the valuation rule. Of the 61 longs the rules flagged on 26 Oct, 29 did not survive diligence; shorts are scarce because most cash-burning biotechs trade below, not above, their risk-adjusted value, so each therapeutic area pairs its best long with the best surviving short leg where one exists. The six-month backtest found that cheap-vs-model has lagged (29 prior long picks with history returned a median -24% against -13.6% for the universe), so every pick needs a catalyst, not just a discount.

Returns are share-price changes from the frozen ledger price to the current price (no dividends; takeover jumps are included). Benchmarks: XBI price return and the median of all covered names (equal-weight small caps usually differ from cap-weighted XBI).

signals.title: Earning revenue
signals.why: Companies that already earn a profit were the only group with positive median returns.

signals.title: Market cap at the start of the window
signals.why: Larger companies fell less; micro-caps carried the pain.

signals.title: Development stage
signals.why: The market paid for de-risked, near-commercial assets.

signals.title: Pipeline breadth
signals.why: Single-asset stories were punished; breadth cushioned setbacks.

signals.title: Crowding of the indication
signals.why: Indications with many competing programs de-rated more than niche ones.

2026-10.method: Best long per TA: LONG/STRONG BUY with upside >0, passing the top-pick tests when any does, ranked by upside (capped at 400%) x PoS weight x science score. Best short per TA: SHORT/STRONG SHORT (else AVOID) with upside <= -20% and market cap >= $150M; borrow cost and squeeze risk are NOT assessed. "Priced in" solves for the PoS (or peak sales) that makes our NPV plus cash equal today's market cap, holding every other input fixed.

rev.edition: Revised 27 Oct 2026 (originally published 13 Oct: 81 highlighted picks, 63 by rule)
rev.headline: Rule-based picks after diligence and a skeptical red-team pass (27 Oct): 18 committee-shortlist longs, 35 other top longs, 3 top short and 8 pair shorts (diligence-confirmed short legs), plus 9 analyst nominees. Red-teaming the ten highest-conviction longs demoted 47 of them: elite status now requires surviving the strongest bear case, not just the valuation rule. Of the 61 longs the rules flagged on 26 Oct, 29 did not survive diligence; shorts are scarce because most cash-burning biotechs trade below, not above, their risk-adjusted value, so each therapeutic area pairs its best long with the best surviving short leg where one exists. The six-month backtest found that cheap-vs-model has lagged (29 prior long picks with history returned a median -24% against -13.6% for the universe), so every pick needs a catalyst, not just a discount.

lessons.title: Cheap-vs-model catches falling knives
lessons.insight: Valuation says where a stock can go; it does not say when. A cheap-vs-model rule needs a trigger (dated catalyst, revenue inflection, insider or balance-sheet support) before it earns full size.
lessons.evidence: 29 current rule-based longs with history returned a median -24% over Apr 24-Oct 26 vs -13.6% for the 312-name universe (UPB -70%, NKTR -59%, OLMA -57%, GPCR -54%).
lessons.action: Picks down 25%+ in 3 months are tagged with a warning marker; size them smaller until a catalyst or stabilization appears. Fundamentals still set the destination.

lessons.title: Trading near cash is not a floor
lessons.insight: Names at or below cash kept falling when nothing forced a re-rating: the market was pricing cash burn and financing, not the asset.
lessons.evidence: UPB (-70%), LYEL (-58%), TRDA (-57%) all traded near cash and kept sliding; REPL and ACHV worked because a regulatory path to a reset existed.
lessons.action: A below-cash long needs (a) a dated catalyst, (b) runway beyond it, (c) no pending raise at a discount.

lessons.title: What actually worked as longs
lessons.insight: Two repeatable archetypes: cheap commercial compounders that kept beating and raising, and validated mechanisms with a dated catalyst and cash.
lessons.evidence: Compounders (HALO, CORT, KNSA, IOVA, XERS, ADPT, RIGL, GMAB): median +83%. Validated + dated catalyst + cash (VRDN, SLN, MBX, ABCL, AMLX, KOD, DFTX): median +100%. n is small and selected from top movers.
lessons.action: Add a commercial-inflection long screen (revenue growth, guidance raises, EV/sales) next to the pipeline-value screen.

lessons.title: What worked as shorts, and what it cost
lessons.insight: Shorts that paid were run-ups into binary readouts with weak priors (and fades of post-data spikes). They are still coin flips with squeeze tails; none was a clean ex-ante call.
lessons.evidence: TENX -90%, EVMN -80%, ELTX -71%, MPLT -73%, NKTR -59% after a spike. Counter-lessons: SPRO fell 61% after FDA approval (a short into the PDUFA was not defensible); SLS has ~30% of float short.
lessons.rejected: 2026-10-26 second look at five run-up shorts, all rejected: SLS (undated readout, ~26% borrow fee, retail buyout chatter), FATE (near cash, no dated binary), DMRA (data mid-2027, $540M cash), TTRX (catalyst is enrollment, not a readout; stage 1 looked positive), ABSI (Lilly stake, takeover risk, interim only "2H26").
lessons.action: Short only with a dated catalyst, positive carry/borrow checked, and a stop; never short pending M&A (SUPN) or stale-cash names (ANL).

lessons.title: Dashboard inputs go stale fastest on cash, catalysts and stage
lessons.insight: Diligence changed at least one fact on 72 of 74 top-pick names. Cash was wrong in both directions (ANL $232M not $24M; NKTR $1.02B not $569M; VCRE $93M not $323M).
lessons.evidence: Changelog 2026-10-26: cash 51, catalyst 50, runway 39, PoS 35, catalyst date 32, stage_full 28, stage 5.
lessons.action: Never act on a pick without re-checking the latest 10-Q cash, runway and catalyst date; rerun diligence after each earnings season.

lessons.title: Some of the biggest moves were not predictable
lessons.insight: Takeovers and post-failure bleeds drove several of the largest moves with no sound ex-ante case.
lessons.evidence: 0 of 60 big movers were a clean ex-ante call; 15 had no sound ex-ante case; NRIX (Roche deal), SLN (later bid).
lessons.action: Treat takeover premium as upside optionality, never as the thesis. Keep sizing to survive being wrong.

lessons.title: Verification capacity is a constraint
lessons.insight: The research agents share a web-search allowance; large parallel batches run out partway and leave drivers unverified.
lessons.evidence: Second-pass idea generation covered about 19 of 260 names; backtest drivers marked unverified for CNXU, CRBU, LENZ, TRDA.
lessons.action: Run diligence in smaller sequential waves; do not cite 'unverified' fields.

backtest.method: 30 biggest winners and 30 biggest decliners among 312 names (price>=$2, mkt cap>=$100M, >=$1M daily volume); each researched for what was public BEFORE the move.
backtest.caveat: Selected from extremes: shows what was identifiable, not a hit rate. No point-in-time ledger exists before Sep 2026 so the dashboard rules cannot be back-tested.

cases.one_line: Below-cash entry after 2nd CRL with prior FDA-reversal precedent; +431% to approval but the May-29 FDA path reset was unforeseeable. Partial edge.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Post-CRL the stock traded at or below cash (~$269M) despite 3-yr IGNYTE OS data and prior FDA reversal precedent; management/FDA dialogue was ongoing. Skeptical view: second CRL cited single-arm design, BMO PT $1, burn ~$70M/qtr, going-concern risk. Option-like long: cash floor ~partially eroded, upside needs FDA path. PoS of reversal low (~15-25%), payoff 4-5x.
cases.tradability: Liquid: ~10M sh/day (~$25M/day) at entry. Short float ~25.7% in Oct 2026 (Finviz via third party) - squeeze-prone, helped long. Large drawdowns inside hold (Jul 24->Jul 28 -45%) though entry-based MAE tiny.

cases.one_line: Binary wet-AMD Ph3 readout with validated molecule; +177% on win. Positive-EV setup but a coin flip - EYPT failed the same week class of trial.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Wet AMD noninferiority vs Eylea is a lower-bar endpoint and GLOW2 had validated the molecule, but KOD's history includes mixed prior pivotal results (unverified specifics) and a 2023 cataract/safety halt. Stock fell ~27% into the readout, which pared the run-up. PoS noninferiority maybe 50-60%; upside 2-3x, downside -40-50%. Positive EV but a binary.
cases.tradability: Avg volume ~0.77M sh/day (~$25M/day) pre-data; fine for small funds. Post-move cap ~$5.6B; equity raise likely.

cases.one_line: Cheap royalty-cliff-discounted profitable large cap with 3 late assets; +66% over 6 months but catalysts unverified. Reasonable thesis, edge modest.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Large-cap, profitable royalty-funded biotech with 3 late-stage assets (Epkinly, Rina-S, petosemtamab) valued as if royalty cliff in 2029 consumed everything; sell-side upgrade at 26.87. Low-risk, diversified quality-value long but the +66% required pipeline news flow that was not predictable in size.
cases.tradability: Very liquid ADR, ~$58M/day. Not a short candidate.

cases.one_line: Short into wet-AMD Ph3: coin flip pre-LUGANO (won); the post-miss short into correlated LUCIA was the more defensible leg.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Pre-LUGANO: $1B+ valuation priced a high PoS for a first-in-class TKI insert in a noninferiority Ph3 vs Eylea, with consensus PTs ~$40; two independent pivotals must both win (joint PoS maybe 50-60%). Shorting before binary has negative skew from squeeze risk. A better short existed after the LUGANO miss into LUCIA (correlated).
cases.tradability: Liquid pre-event (~$10M+/day); borrow/short interest unverified; gap risk on binary was large both ways.

cases.one_line: Ph2b readout short on run-up (+28% pre-data) paid +80%, but outcome was binary; modest base-rate edge only (Ph2b ~30% PoS).
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Short a recent-IPO, unvalidated-mechanism Ph2b name that ran +28% into readout; Ph2b success base rate ~30-35%, so skew negative. But shorting binary ahead of data with squeeze/gap-up risk and strong cash (>2yr) is a coin flip, not an edge.
cases.tradability: ~$9M/day; small-cap recent IPO; borrow/short interest unverified; high squeeze risk around data.

cases.one_line: Shorting an 80%-collapsed post-failure microcap: no verifiable ex-ante case, drivers of May-Oct decline unknown; treat as hindsight.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: No sound ex-ante short identifiable from what I could verify: post-failure names usually trade near cash, making shorts a poor-risk trade (liquidation/strategic-alternative bids cause squeezes; 7/27 +46%). Any thesis (cash burn, no pipeline) was already priced after an 80% collapse.
cases.tradability: Poor: ~$2.5M/day, micro-cap ($178M), shorts would face borrow and squeeze risk.

cases.one_line: IOVA: cheap-vs-growth commercial rerating (Q2 beat, FY guide raise); +288% from post-Q1. Edge was valuation, not timing; big rally partly momentum.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Commercial TIL therapy priced ~3-4x run-rate sales with 3 years cash, 41% GM improving, guidance implying H2 ramp. Skeptic: guidance-based, capacity constrained, interim CEO, history of dilution; edge = cheap growth, not a catalyst. PoS of beat-and-raise moderate (~50%).
cases.tradability: Liquid: ~$53M avg daily $ volume at start, ~$1.5B cap. Easy to size. Run was retail/momentum-heavy (Stocktwits 'extremely bullish', buyout chatter unverified); no short-interest data found.

cases.one_line: HALO: ~8x fwd P/E growth royalty co with buyback; Q2 beat/raise and Merck injunction doubled it. Valuation edge visible, timing not.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Royalty compounder with visible 2026 guide and an 8x forward P/E, heavy buyback, so multiple was pricing a patent/IRA cliff. Beat-and-raise or litigation win re-rates. Risk: Merck/IRA binary overhangs. Edge = valuation gap; timing uncertain.
cases.tradability: Highly liquid (~$120M ADV, ~$7.4B cap). No borrow issue; long only.

cases.one_line: RIGL: profitable ~2x-sales small cap, steady guide raises plus VEPPANU add; +78%. Cheap-quality thesis, no single catalyst; drivers partly unverified.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Profitable small cap at ~2x revenue with R289 optionality and likely portfolio additions; low-risk value long. Risks: Gavreto decline, cash drawdown for in-licensing, thin float. Edge modest, no dated catalyst.
cases.tradability: Smaller/illiquid: ~$12.8M ADV, ~$0.57B cap; sizing limited. Long only.

cases.one_line: KPTI: short into mid-2026 Phase 3 with going concern; +93% short P&L. Event binary; the cleaner trade was shorting the post-failure debt-deadline slide.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Short into binary: post-hoc subgroup confirmation trials fail more often than not, but the stock priced only a fraction of upside (cap ~$160M) and a win would have cured the going concern. Downside to near-zero if fail; upside maybe +100-200%. Asymmetry arguable but binary.
cases.tradability: Hard: ~$3.7M ADV, tiny cap, going concern; likely hard-to-borrow and high squeeze risk into topline; upside gap risk large. Shorting after the failure was easier (cheap to borrow unknown).

cases.one_line: CNXU: new-listing decay -77%; drivers unverified, short faced -29% squeeze first. Cannot claim ex-ante case.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Unverified. Generic: newly listed small cap with thin float and lockup/ supply overhang tends to drift down, but a short on day 1 would have faced a -29% adverse squeeze to 16.85 before paying off.
cases.tradability: Poor: ~$1.3M ADV, ~$0.37M-0.37B cap, multiple 12-27% squeeze days; borrow unverified.

cases.one_line: LENZ: -60% post-gap slow bleed after -21% day; drivers unverified (search limit), trend-follow short only. Screen's STRONG BUY was wrong.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Weak: price momentum plus launch-slippage risk. Without the verified launch data, a short on 05-12 after the gap is a trend-following trade, not a fundamental catalyst call. Edge modest; the gap itself was not predictable.
cases.tradability: Moderate: ~$7.8M ADV, ~$0.29B cap; borrow unverified.

cases.one_line: Scheduled Ph2 in a validated mechanism, cash-rich but already doubled: reasonable binary long that paid +49% (partial edge, not clear).
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Long into a scheduled, date-certain Ph2 in a mechanism already validated by two approved small molecules; long-acting antibody is differentiated and $565M cash limits financing risk. But stock doubled YTD and ran +32% into print; EV ~$1.6B prices high PoS. Positive EV only if you believed PoS >~75%; dilution after data was predictable.
cases.tradability: Highly liquid (~$46M avg daily $ vol at entry per batch; 6.8M shares/day pre-print, 46M on event day). Gap-up of +35% on the event means pre-event entry was the only way to capture it; post-event buyer got only the further +11% by 08-12. Short interest unverified.

cases.one_line: Post-approval launch under-modelled; Q1 guidance raise then Q2 beat doubled stock. Defensible but not certain; Genmab ADC hit gave back ~29% from peak.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Approved-early oncology drug into an NCCN-preferred slot, with a profitable cash-generating base, at ~5x revenue after a CRL-driven -50% reset. Launch trajectory and Cushing's resubmission offered two catalysts (Q1/Q2 prints, Dec PDUFA). Edge: launches that start 'vigorous' tend to be under-modelled early. Weakness: Korlym generic erosion and no launch data yet at entry.
cases.tradability: Liquid: ~$67M/day dollar volume at entry (batch), 0.6-1.5M shares/day. Mid-cap ($5B). Easy to size; shorts not relevant.

cases.one_line: Pivot-to-acne plus a $6 financing triggered +39% gap; no public signal pre-4/24 supported entry; post-event drift (Barclays, IND) was the more tradable part.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Weak. A sub-$450M company with ~$113M cash and an unfunded MASH Ph3 had a positive foreign acne Ph3 that could be leveraged, but nothing public said Sagimet would pivot or raise on 04-27. The offering priced at $6.00 (2% above the close), so only deal participants captured the pop. Outsider long at 5.86 was a bet on an undisclosed corporate action.
cases.tradability: Liquid (~$29M/day dollar vol at entry); gap-up +38.6% on event day means only pre-announcement or in-deal participation captured it. Dilution of ~29M shares at $6 and again $115M at $10 on 09-30.

cases.one_line: Pre-readout short after +34% run into a guided Ph2a: sound valuation logic, but binary; -91% on a miss. Not repeatable edge, so coin flip with a skew.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Short a ~$2.2B pre-efficacy biotech one session before a guided binary on an add-on mechanism that must beat a very effective SoC; stock had rallied 34% into the print, cash only ~12% of cap. Edge is valuation vs low base-rate PoS (Ph2 add-on, novel NBD1 mechanism) but outcome binary and a success could be +30-50%.
cases.tradability: Mid-cap (~$16M/day dollar volume at entry per batch, 0.3-1.1M shares/day) - borrow availability, short interest and squeeze risk unverified. Event gap -91% in one session; position sizing must tolerate a +30-50% gap against.

cases.one_line: -77% window decline concentrated on 10-07/08; cause unverified, no verified public pre-signal beyond downtrend and volume uptick: treat as hindsight-only.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Cannot be established from verified public data. Only observable: persistent downtrend and unusual volume the day before. A skeptical short thesis (cash burn, allogeneic CAR-T dilution, sub-$1.50 stock) could have existed but the event driver is unknown, so no ex-ante edge is claimed.
cases.tradability: Small cap, ~$3.2M/day dollar volume; sub-$1.50 stock; borrow cost, locate and squeeze risk unverified; extreme gap-down on 10-07 means a short entered after the open captured little. Sub-$1 price raises Nasdaq minimum-bid issues.

cases.one_line: -57% gap on 05-07 then continued bleed to 4.75; driver unverified, only a pre-event run-up/volume signal: classify hindsight-only pending news check.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: No verifiable ex-ante thesis. If the 05-07 move was a scheduled data readout, a short after a +26% run-up was a binary bet; if it was an unscheduled event (partner/regulatory), it was unpredictable. Cannot determine without the news source.
cases.tradability: ~$5.7M/day dollar volume at 04-24; ~140-600K shares/day before event - thin; borrow, short interest and squeeze risk unverified. Gap of -57% overnight leaves no time to enter post-news.

cases.one_line: Buy before Aug Ph2 PV readout (Cantor 75% PoS vs <25% implied): +122% on data; later Merck KGaA bid was unpredictable bonus. Partial case.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Dated catalyst (Aug Ph2) for a placebo-controlled, phlebotomy-dependent PV trial with a clinically-validated mechanism (rusfertide class) and encouraging Ph1; ~$300M cap for a lead asset in a rare disease. Base-rate Ph2 PoS for a validated mechanism ~50-60%; Cantor 75%. Risks: small n=48, cash ~$70M, raise on success. Positive skew if cap ~2x cash and PoS >50%.
cases.tradability: Long: avg dollar volume ~ $1.7M/day at entry price scale (batch dv), market cap ~$460M at 4/24 -> position sizing limited; ADS liquidity thin until the Aug 10 spike (16M sh). Acceptable for a small fund.

cases.one_line: Growth/compounder long after the 5/5 beat-and-raise: +91% via guide raises, MRD/Immune Medicine split plan and a re-rating. Reasonable thesis, magnitude not predictable.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Consistent 40%+ volume growth, MRD profitable, guidance raised, ~$2.3B cap (~5.5x 2026E total revenue of ~$300M) with an unprofitable Immune Medicine arm masking MRD value; sum-of-parts / separation catalyst plausible. Not a binary; edge is compounding growth plus likelihood of continued beats. Valuation vs Natera/Guardant MRD peers a debate; PoS of beat-and-raise high but multiple expansion not assured.
cases.tradability: Long: $23M/day dollar volume, ~$2.3B cap at entry - fully liquid. Short (screen's call) would have had MAE of ~+110% to the 10/5 high.

cases.one_line: Post-PIPE long on a pre-announced CRL with efficacy intact: +63% to window end (peak +112%). Well-reasoned but approval not yet realized.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: CRL was already telegraphed (OAI) so the 'bad news' was in the price; fully funded by the $180M PIPE and stock near the PIPE price of $3.635 acts as a soft floor; efficacy/safety package was approved-quality, so the path to approval is CMC only. Upside as CRL clears overhang and resubmission nears; downside limited to PIPE price (~-10%). Base rate: CMC-only CRLs resubmitted with new site are approved >80% of the time but timing slips.
cases.tradability: Long: ~$6M/day dollar volume, $413M cap at entry; PIPE shares/warrants (up to ~99M share overhang after registration) could cap upside. Reasonable size for small fund.

cases.one_line: Pre-efficacy oncology name at ~4-5x cash fell 89%; driver of the 6/15 crash unverified, no dated catalyst - cannot call it ex-ante.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Valuation of ~$210M for a pre-efficacy oncology platform with ~$50-60M cash and rising burn implies a financing/dilution event or a disappointing early readout; but no dated negative catalyst was identifiable, and early-phase small caps frequently squeeze on any data. Short would have needed to sit through +32% adverse excursion. Cause of the 6/15 -51% not verified.
cases.tradability: Short: ~$1.7M/day dollar volume, tiny float-cap; borrow likely hard/expensive (unverified); high squeeze risk (+13% day on 5/27, MAE +32%). After the stock fell sub-$1 liquidity improved only on the way down.

cases.one_line: Short into Ph2 binary after a 35% run-up: -73% on 7/27 when QD dose missed. Directionally right but a coin-flip bet, not an identifiable edge.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Run-up of ~35% into a single Ph2 binary left ~$2B cap pricing a clean win; muscarinic schizophrenia trials have mixed record (emraclidine fail, high placebo response) and a once-daily dose was the differentiating claim. Asymmetric if PoS of clean success <50%, but a positive print could mean +30% and shorts get squeezed; sizing must be small. Truly a coin flip.
cases.tradability: Short: ~$8M/day dollar volume, ~$1.65B cap; borrow availability/short interest unverified; gap risk 70%+ on failure and +30%+ on success.

cases.one_line: Post-EMA-withdrawal drift short at 2.4x cash: -62% by 10/26 as stock fell below cash-ish levels. Defensible but no dated catalyst; drivers of later legs unverified.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: After the EU withdrawal the lead asset had no regulatory path outside a new, costly trial; stock still ~2.4x cash. Expect drift lower toward cash as hype fades, absent a catalyst; but price already -50% from YTD high and retail/hype squeezes (MAE +6.6% only, but spike risk) make it a modest-edge drift trade, not a dated catalyst.
cases.tradability: Short: ~$2.8M/day dollar volume, ~$309M cap, retail-heavy; borrow/short-interest unverified; squeeze risk elevated (8/25 +14.5% day).

cases.one_line: Long SLS from 5/12 to 11.54 (+121%) on REGAL event-count run-up; no readout yet, so pure catalyst-anticipation, not an ex-ante-clear edge.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Event-driven momentum long into a pending Phase 3 OS readout. Small-cap AML vaccine maintenance trial with a historically low Phase 3 base rate (~25-35%) and a $5 stock already carrying ~$900M cap; positive carry came from catalyst-run-up dynamics (80th event, cash raised via warrants), not a mispricing. Long = run-up trade only; holding through unblinding is a coin flip.
cases.tradability: Liquid: ~$57M/day dollar volume at entry window; ATM and warrant overhang continuous (shares +32% in 6 months). Short interest not found. Retail-driven, so shorting this was a squeeze trap (tool flagged 'STRONG SHORT'; stock +154%).

cases.one_line: Long HELP from 6/24 to 10.19 (+100%) on Q4 pivotal-readout run-up, sector M&A and CEO hire; thesis not yet tested by data, so only partial ex-ante edge.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Small-cap psychedelic with Breakthrough designation, an imminent pivotal readout (Q4), cash for Phase 3, and a depressed ~$4-5 price after a 6-month drawdown. Long a pre-binary run-up; sector M&A and catalysts (enrollment complete, CEO hire) were plausible momentum drivers. Phase 3 PoS in MDD adjunctive psychedelic ~40-50%, placebo/functional-unblinding risk high.
cases.tradability: Thin-ish: ~$4.9M/day dollar volume at window start; $410M cap. Volume spikes 5-15x on catalyst days; $50M equity raise indicates dilution risk. Nov readout still pending at window end.

cases.one_line: Long DRTS 5/7 to 13.16 (+68%) on a drip of pivotal-enrollment and trial updates; plausible catalyst flow but no decisive ex-ante edge.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Device-like radiotherapy platform with Breakthrough designation and a pivotal single-arm trial near full enrollment; catalysts (PMA completion, enrollment milestones, multiple small-trial readouts) are frequent but each is low-information. Edge is thematic (multiple shots on goal) rather than a defined mispricing; single-arm data and ATM overhang limit conviction.
cases.tradability: Illiquid-ish: ~$9M/day, ~$770M cap at window start; ATM overhang; grinding drift allows scaling in. Max adverse from 5/7 entry was 0 at close but -13.6% from 5/11 (10.34) to 6/2 (8.93).

cases.one_line: Short TENX into LEVEL Phase 3 (8/7 at 13.44 -> 1.38, +90%); thesis (run-up priced in success, weak Ph2) was valid but outcome was a binary.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Cap ~$500M on a single drug whose Phase 2 supporting data came from IV dosing and responder enrichment with a missed primary endpoint. Phase 3 6MWD endpoints in HFpEF-PH historically fail often (PoS ~20-30%). Price implied near-certain success after a +70% run-up; short or put-spread into the August readout had positive EV but payoff was a pure binary with squeeze risk.
cases.tradability: Borrow likely available at entry (short interest only ~2.6M shares, ~8% of shares on 7/31); ~$9M/day. Warrants-heavy base raises gap risk; short interest then surged to 14.7% by 9/15 and 21.7% of float now.

cases.one_line: Short ALMS into Q3 LUMUS lupus readout (8/31 21.81 -> 6.78, +69%); known binary, overvalued lupus option, but 50/50 outcome.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: At ~$22, EV about $2.7B on an oral TYK2 whose psoriasis efficacy is only comparable to deucravacitinib; much of the premium rested on SLE optionality with a known Q3 binary. Phase 2b SLE success rates are modest (~40-50%), and IFNGS stratification risk was visible. Short or hedge into LUMUS had negative skew only if you believe market overpaid; otherwise coin-flip.
cases.tradability: Cap $3.2B, ~$22M/day, borrow likely easy; short interest not found. Risk was gap-up on success (+30-50%) vs downside ~-55%.

cases.one_line: Short ADCT into LOTIS-5 (6/3 3.08 -> 0.98, +68%); trial hit PFS but deaths killed it, so the short won for an unforeseeable reason.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: No sound short case on the efficacy endpoint: a Phase 3 add-on to an approved ADC had decent odds of hitting PFS (it did). Downside came from a safety/OS surprise that was not predictable from public data. A short into binary data on a $500M cap with approved revenue would have been a coin flip with squeezing risk.
cases.tradability: ~$4M/day dollar volume, ~$500M cap, NYSE; borrow and short interest unverified; after the collapse the stock was sub-$1.50 with high borrow/penny-stock risk.

cases.one_line: ABSI +140% from the 4/24 low: Phase 1 safety data + Lilly-backed $100M raise; no sound ex-ante case found for the low entry.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Cash-burning AI-drug-discovery name with one clinical asset (ABS-201) and a PoC readout in H2 2026. A skeptical analyst sees an unvalidated mechanism, financing overhang and no hard catalyst on 4/24; a bull case needs momentum/Lilly-backed validation. No sound edge visible before the 4/27 gap.
cases.tradability: Long: ~$14M/day dollar volume in the 20d before 4/24, ~$676M cap; fine for small size. A 4/24 entry sits exactly at the window low (MAE 0) which is hindsight. Short interest 24% of float, 9 days to cover (Oct 2026) so squeeze-prone for shorts.

cases.one_line: KNSA +67%: two beat-and-raise ARCALYST prints (4/28, 7/28) drove it; defensible growth-at-reasonable-price long, but magnitude of re-rating needed luck.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Profitable single-product growth story with a beat-and-raise cadence. Guide of $900-920M looked conservative against 50%+ growth; consensus lagged the demand trend. Long into Q1 print for a likely beat/raise plus KPL-387 optionality. Edge is modest (earnings reaction magnitude uncertain) but risk/reward was favourable.
cases.tradability: Long: ~$31M/day dollar volume (20d avg), ~$3.3B cap; highly liquid. Insiders own ~52%, float modest.

cases.one_line: AMLX +64% on LUCIDITY Ph3 win (55% event cut, p=3e-6); good de-risked profile but still a binary with a prior Ph3-failure history; PARTIAL.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Phase 3 in rare, endpoint-objective indication after two positive Phase 2s, BTD, FDA-agreed endpoint, coherent mechanism: PoS maybe 65-75% vs market-implied lower after a 2024 Relyvrio failure hangover; cash ~$250M vs ~$2.1B cap at 4/24 (cap lower in May). Binary event with stock already +68% off the May low into data.
cases.tradability: Long: ~$42M/day dollar volume, ~$2.1B cap; very liquid. Run-up of +68% from 5/19 low means the entry on 8/17 had already priced in some success.

cases.one_line: ELTX short into AMPLIFY-7P readout: -71% on miss. Sound thesis (run-up, thin cash, base rates) but still a binary with a squeeze tail.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Micro-cap with <6 months cash, only single-arm Phase 1 evidence, a differently-formulated (7P) construct, and a +62% three-week run into a binary DFS readout. Cancer-vaccine PoS maybe 25-30%; stock at ~$300M cap implied far more. Short/avoid or buy puts; a positive readout would give ~+100% squeeze, so risk is not asymmetric.
cases.tradability: Poor: ~$1.7M/day dollar volume, ~$300M cap at entry; borrow likely scarce and costly; ~9.6% of float short in Oct 2026 (entry-date SI unverified). Options liquidity unknown. Gap risk both ways; ATM/offering risk.

cases.one_line: STRO -77% from 5/15: sell-the-run-up into early Ph1 data (Aug 12) plus an unexplained autumn bleed; plausible bear case but timing is mostly hindsight.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: After a 5x run on a single Phase 1 ADC with early data due mid-year, 'sell the run-up' skew: efficacy early updates seldom live up, anemia/safety signals plausible, cash burn ~$40M/qtr. Entry after first lower-high rollover. Real edge limited; timing luck and no identified catalyst for the May drop.
cases.tradability: Short: ~$8.6M/day dollar volume, ~$550M cap at 4/24; borrow/short interest unverified; run-up momentum names carry squeeze risk, and pre-data shorting is a binary. Entry 5/15 is justified only as the day before the first leg down, which is partly hindsight.

cases.one_line: SPRO -61% despite FDA approval: sell-the-news plus a royalty-pledge financing that subordinated equity; a short into PDUFA was not a defensible ex-ante trade.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Short a stock into a probable approval is hard to defend: efficacy stopped early, partner GSK, and EV near cash plus modest economics. A bear case existed only on 'approval is priced, economics small (1% royalty? unverified), pivot/financing dilution to follow'. Defensible as 'avoid long' not as a short.
cases.tradability: Short: ~$2.5M/day dollar volume at entry, ~$160M cap; sub-$3 stock, borrow cost/availability unverified; any approval-day squeeze risk; ATM and 2x authorized shares signalled dilution.

cases.one_line: First Tracks (AnaptysBio spin-off): +64% to celiac readout, but the 07-09 +56% gap had no identifiable catalyst; timing is hindsight, spin-off discount is the only ex-ante angle.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Spin-off with forced/indifferent holder base trading near cash (~$15-20 vs ~$7/sh cash est.) holding a Phase 2 celiac asset. A patient analyst could own it for the spin-off discount, but the specific 07-09 jump had no visible public trigger, so the entry timing was not derivable.
cases.tradability: Long: mkt cap ~$650M at p0, ~$9.5M/day value traded; entry-day volume ~0.55M sh so a $2-3M position was fine pre-jump; thin after. Post-10-12 private placement is an overhang.

cases.one_line: VRDN into REVEAL-2 + PDUFA: validated mechanism, cash-rich, derated 40% YTD; both events hit, +31% to approval, +66% to window end.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Class-validated IGF-1R mechanism, priority-review PDUFA 6/30, ample cash, and a second Ph3 (REVEAL-2) expected in 2026 with SC dosing. Base PoS for approval ~85-90%, REVEAL-2 hit ~75-80%. Stock -40% YTD with $760M cash suggests asymmetric payoff into two de-risking events.
cases.tradability: Highly liquid: mkt cap ~$1.56B, ~$60M/day. Long needed no special borrow; risk is event/gap risk only.

cases.one_line: Definium Emerge Ph3: pre-announced binary on a strong Ph2b but already +245%/12m; hit, +50% in a day; good outcome, but entry was a coin flip with edge only from PoS.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: Strong Ph2b effect size in GAD makes Ph3 success likely (~65-75% PoS) but unblinding critique and 245% 12-month run mean much was priced. Dated binary with symmetric-ish payoff (+50% up vs probably -40-50% down).
cases.tradability: Mkt cap ~$3.0B, ~$34M/day (2.3M sh/day pre-event); liquid. Binary gap risk; post-win equity raise was ~$700M (reported).

cases.one_line: CMPX short into COMPANION-002: -64% when OS missed (HR 1.05) despite strong PFS; crossover risk was visible but direction of a dated binary was not.
cases.ex_ante_thesis: A skeptic could argue ORR-primary win was priced, with OS, the endpoint FDA cares about, confounded by crossover: asymmetric downside if OS missed. But PFS HR likely strong and approvable, so odds of a gap-down were not clearly better than a rally. Short into a dated binary.

2026-11.headline: November revision (17 Nov). Lead programs and catalysts were re-checked against Q3 reports for all 402 names and balance sheets (cash, debt, fully diluted shares) refreshed for most; the picks list is the rule-based output after diligence and red-team gates of 27 Oct and 4 Nov: 0 elite long, 36 other top longs, 2 top shorts and 2 pair shorts, plus 8 analyst nominees. Lead changes since the last edition include Cullinan (now CLN-978 in autoimmune disease), Aclaris, Arrivent, Bicycle and Foghorn; NeurAxis (a device company) was removed and the universe is held to $50M-$30B market cap (73 names parked). longs.name: Abeona
longs.catalyst: More QTC treatments and revenue ramp; no guided date (Q4 2026 results next)
longs.pitch: Q3 ZEVASKYN sales of $13.5M (+18% q/q, 15 treatments since launch, 8 QTCs) against a $161M cap that is 1.2x cash; surgical-graft logistics and Krystal's convenient VYJUVEK limit the ramp.
longs.bull: Approved product with NTAP, 7 QTCs, cash ~half of market cap; yield normalization would drive ramp beyond ~$11M/qtr.
longs.bear: Only 3 treatments in Q3-to-date as of Aug; yield/lot-release failures defer revenue; ~$20M quarterly loss; ATM available; small patient pool.
longs.risk: Q3 revenue flat/down on yield failures, forcing raise.
longs.wrong: Q3 shows >=5 recognized treatments and yield fix.

rt.bear: Launch is lumpy and tiny: ~12 lifetime treatments by Aug 13, with lot-release/yield failures already deferring revenue. Q3 print (due ~Nov 10) can easily be flat/down; ~$20M+/qtr burn on $147M cash means ATM dilution on any miss. ~750 eligible US patients.
rt.rebut: $3.1M WAC, >95% commercial coverage, 7 QTCs, avg 9 sheets/cycle; mgmt says cash-flow positive above 3 patients/month; cash ~half of market cap.
rt.flip: Q3 revenue clearly >$15M with yield fixed and >3 treatments/month (KEEP); Q3 flat/down or new lot failures (DROP).
errs: Catalyst date 2026-11-10 is the Q3 report date, unverified; no Q3 results found as of 11-04
'3 treatments in Q3 to date' is an Aug 13 figure, stale
Price/mc not re-verified
PoS 1.0 is fine for approved product but says nothing about commercial risk
rt.fin: Cash $146.8M at 6/30; burn ~$20M/qtr gives ~7-8 qtrs on paper but a launch miss triggers ATM use; cash-flow breakeven needs >3 pts/month, not yet shown.

longs.name: Upstream
longs.catalyst: Ph3 starts in severe asthma and CRSwNP planned Q1 2027; COPD Ph2 VENTURE data 2H 2027; cash $207M funds through 2027
longs.pitch: Ph2 VALIANT (n=478) cut exacerbations 56% at 100 mg q12w (p<0.001), yet the cap is $119M vs $207M cash. Cash only funds through 2027, so the ~1,500-patient Ph3 starting Q1 2027 needs a raise or partner.
longs.bull: Negative-EV-ish TSLP-R mAb with q12w dosing, Ph2 hit primary (56% AAER cut at 100mg), single pivotal Ph3 per indication; validated mechanism (Tezspire).
longs.bear: Ph3 dose (400mg) untested vs. 100mg win; low-eos non-response; Ph3 cost exceeds $261M cash, runway only through 2027; dilutive raise likely before/at Ph3 start; launch 2030.
longs.risk: Ph3 financing at or below cash value, or partnering on poor terms.
longs.wrong: Non-dilutive partnership at premium, or Ph3 dose-ranging data showing clean eos-independent efficacy.

rt.bear: The 56% AAER cut is the 100 mg q12w arm; 400 mg q24w gave only 39% (below Tezspire's NAVIGATOR), and Phase 3 will use 400 mg q12w, a regimen not tested in Phase 2. Low-eosinophil patients (<150/uL, ~20% of severe asthma) showed no significant benefit and Phase 3 is unrestricted by biomarker; the 87% eos>=300 figure is a PI-quoted subgroup. Phase 3 (~1,500 pts) costs more than the $261M cash, so a raise or partner is needed first.
rt.rebut: Market cap ~$150M is below $261M cash (negative EV), q12w beats monthly Tezspire, and a partner or takeout would re-rate it.
rt.flip: Partner deal with Ph3 funding, or Ph2 data showing the 400 mg q12w regimen and low-eos benefit.
errs: Pitch's 'q12w vs q4w Tezspire' edge ignores twice-yearly TSLP entrants (WIN378 already in Phase 3)
No mention that the Phase 3 dose (400 mg q12w) was not the Phase 2 winner (100 mg q12w)
Elite status assumed an unrestricted label; low-eosinophil non-response is not in the pitch
rt.fin: Phase 3 cost exceeds $261M cash; raise or partner needed by the Q1'27 start; ATM $150M live.

2026-11.method: Best long per TA: LONG/STRONG BUY with upside >0, passing the top-pick tests when any does, ranked by upside (capped at 400%) x PoS weight x science score. Best short per TA: SHORT/STRONG SHORT (else AVOID) with upside <= -20% and market cap >= $150M; borrow cost and squeeze risk are NOT assessed. "Priced in" solves for the PoS (or peak sales) that makes our NPV plus cash equal today's market cap, holding every other input fixed.

rev.edition: November revision, 17 Nov 2026: prices (16 Nov close), Q3 balance sheets, lead programs and catalysts refreshed for the whole universe. Performance (27 Oct ledger to 17 Nov), the 17 Nov to 17 Dec catalyst calendar and the theme charts are rolled forward by roll_memo.py and roll_themes.py; catalyst-outcome statistics, playbook lessons and backtest are carried over from the 26 Oct edition.
rev.headline: November revision (17 Nov). Lead programs and catalysts were re-checked against Q3 reports for all 402 names and balance sheets (cash, debt, fully diluted shares) refreshed for most; the picks list is the rule-based output after diligence and red-team gates of 27 Oct and 4 Nov: 0 elite long, 36 other top longs, 2 top shorts and 2 pair shorts, plus 8 analyst nominees. Lead changes since the last edition include Cullinan (now CLN-978 in autoimmune disease), Aclaris, Arrivent, Bicycle and Foghorn; NeurAxis (a device company) was removed and the universe is held to $50M-$30B market cap (73 names parked). Rank agreement for the value screen was about zero (Spearman -0.02 over 309 liquid names), so it remains a screen of where to look, not a decision. Not refreshed: holder lists (13F data not yet sourced), XBI after 9 Nov, and the catalyst-outcome statistics, lessons and backtest below, which are from the 26 Oct edition (backtest window 24 Apr to 26 Oct).

lessons.title: Cheap-vs-model catches falling knives
lessons.insight: Valuation says where a stock can go; it does not say when. A cheap-vs-model rule needs a trigger (dated catalyst, revenue inflection, insider or balance-sheet support) before it earns full size.
lessons.evidence: 29 current rule-based longs with history returned a median -24% over Apr 24-Oct 26 vs -13.6% for the 312-name universe (UPB -70%, NKTR -59%, OLMA -57%, GPCR -54%).
lessons.action: Picks down 25%+ in 3 months are tagged with a warning marker; size them smaller until a catalyst or stabilization appears. Fundamentals still set the destination.

lessons.title: Trading near cash is not a floor
lessons.insight: Names at or below cash kept falling when nothing forced a re-rating: the market was pricing cash burn and financing, not the asset.
lessons.evidence: UPB (-70%), LYEL (-58%), TRDA (-57%) all traded near cash and kept sliding; REPL and ACHV worked because a regulatory path to a reset existed.
lessons.action: A below-cash long needs (a) a dated catalyst, (b) runway beyond it, (c) no pending raise at a discount.

lessons.title: What actually worked as longs
lessons.insight: Two repeatable archetypes: cheap commercial compounders that kept beating and raising, and validated mechanisms with a dated catalyst and cash.
lessons.evidence: Compounders (HALO, CORT, KNSA, IOVA, XERS, ADPT, RIGL, GMAB): median +83%. Validated + dated catalyst + cash (VRDN, SLN, MBX, ABCL, AMLX, KOD, DFTX): median +100%. n is small and selected from top movers.
lessons.action: Add a commercial-inflection long screen (revenue growth, guidance raises, EV/sales) next to the pipeline-value screen.

lessons.title: What worked as shorts, and what it cost
lessons.insight: Shorts that paid were run-ups into binary readouts with weak priors (and fades of post-data spikes). They are still coin flips with squeeze tails; none was a clean ex-ante call.
lessons.evidence: TENX -90%, EVMN -80%, ELTX -71%, MPLT -73%, NKTR -59% after a spike. Counter-lessons: SPRO fell 61% after FDA approval (a short into the PDUFA was not defensible); SLS has ~30% of float short.
lessons.rejected: 2026-10-26 second look at five run-up shorts, all rejected: SLS (undated readout, ~26% borrow fee, retail buyout chatter), FATE (near cash, no dated binary), DMRA (data mid-2027, $540M cash), TTRX (catalyst is enrollment, not a readout; stage 1 looked positive), ABSI (Lilly stake, takeover risk, interim only "2H26").
lessons.action: Short only with a dated catalyst, positive carry/borrow checked, and a stop; never short pending M&A (SUPN) or stale-cash names (ANL).

lessons.title: Dashboard inputs go stale fastest on cash, catalysts and stage
lessons.insight: Diligence changed at least one fact on 72 of 74 top-pick names. Cash was wrong in both directions (ANL $232M not $24M; NKTR $1.02B not $569M; VCRE $93M not $323M).
lessons.evidence: Changelog 2026-10-26: cash 51, catalyst 50, runway 39, PoS 35, catalyst date 32, stage_full 28, stage 5.
lessons.action: Never act on a pick without re-checking the latest 10-Q cash, runway and catalyst date; rerun diligence after each earnings season.

lessons.title: Some of the biggest moves were not predictable
lessons.insight: Takeovers and post-failure bleeds drove several of the largest moves with no sound ex-ante case.
lessons.evidence: 0 of 60 big movers were a clean ex-ante call; 15 had no sound ex-ante case; NRIX (Roche deal), SLN (later bid).
lessons.action: Treat takeover premium as upside optionality, never as the thesis. Keep sizing to survive being wrong.

lessons.title: Verification capacity is a constraint
lessons.insight: The research agents share a web-search allowance; large parallel batches run out partway and leave drivers unverified.
lessons.evidence: Second-pass idea generation covered about 19 of 260 names; backtest drivers marked unverified for CNXU, CRBU, LENZ, TRDA. The 6 Nov light check of 115 names mostly returned headlines: 'none found' means unverified.
lessons.action: Run diligence in smaller sequential waves; do not cite 'unverified' fields.

lessons.title: Stale cash and share counts distort the screen
lessons.insight: Cash and diluted shares drive the ratio; IPOs, raises and reverse mergers after the last balance sheet can move cash by 10x.
lessons.evidence: 6 Nov checks: OBX cash $34M to $355M, LTGO $55M to $401M, AMLX $251M to $768M, RAPP $395M to $806M.
lessons.action: Re-verify cash and shares from the latest 10-Q/8-K before trusting any below-cash flag.

backtest.method: 30 biggest winners and 30 biggest decliners among 312 names (price>=$2, mkt cap>=$100M, >=$1M daily volume); each researched for what was public BEFORE the move.
backtest.caveat: Selected from extremes: shows what was identifiable, not a hit rate. No point-in-time ledger exists before Sep 2026 so the dashboard rules cannot be back-tested.
